1  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 18.03.2020 PASSED IN MVC NO.514/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC, MACT, SIRA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION
THIS APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT 1.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 18.03.2020 passed in MVC.No.514/2017 by Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Sira (for short the 'Tribunal') the present appeal is filed by the petitioner therein for enhancement of compensation awarded.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 18.03.2020 at about 8.00 a.m., the petitioner was standing at the left side of the Sira - Madhugiri Road near Ullas Thopu, at that time, a bike bearing registration No.KA.64.H.4606 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner, because of which, which the petitioner sustained the following injury:
 i. Fracture of right humorous.
 ii. 2 simple injuries.
 iii. in patient for 8 days.
 iv. Underwent surgery and in plaints were put  v. disability at 30% to the limb 10% to the whole body but  finding is at 7%.
4.

The Tribunal based on the evidence let-in came to the conclusion that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the bike which was duly insured with respondent No.2 and respondent No.2 is liable to pay a sum of Rs.1,90,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realization under the following heads:
 SL.NO. HEADS OF AMOUNT IN RS.
 COMPENSATION  1. Pain and suffering 15,000
2 . Medical expenses 20,972  3. Attendant charges 6,000  4. Conveyance charges 5,000
5. Food, diet and nourishment 5,000  charges

6. Loss of income during 8,000  treatment  7. Loss of future earning 2,07,360  capacity on account of  permanent physical disability Nagendra C G vs Chandra on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101735206/
2  8. Loss of amenities & 10,000  enjoyment of life  9. Loss of income during 8,000  treatment  10. For permanent disability 1,14,240  11. Amenities 5,000  12.
Future medical expenses 10,000
Not satisfied by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
6. Admittedly, the accident occurred in the year 2017.
The income of the petitioner has not been established before the Tribunal.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok- Adalath chart has to be considered, which will be Rs.11,000/- per month.
The petitioner was aged 26 years at the time of accident.
Given the nature of injury, and evidence let in, I am of the opinion that it would be just and fair to consider the total body disability at 10%.

Given the age of petitioner, the multiplier of 17 has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs.
D.T.C [2009(6) SCC 121], thus the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.2,24,400/-
(Rs.11,000x12x17x10%) towards 'loss of future income' as against Rs.1,14,240/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Given the nature of injuries, the laid up period has to be considered as 2 months and the loss of income during the laid up period will be Rs.22,000/- (Rs.11,000x2) as against Rs.8,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
Towards pain and suffering, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.20,000/-.
Towards medical expenses, based on the actual bills, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,972.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards the head 'Attendant charges', a sum of Rs.6,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal and same is retained.
Towards 'Conveyance', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/-.
I deem it fit to enhance the same to Rs.10,000/-.
Towards 'Food and diet', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/-.
I deem it fit to enhance the same to Rs.5,000/-.
Towards loss of amenities, a sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal, which I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.10,000.
Towards 'Future Medical expenses', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem the same to be appropriate.

Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.3,33,372/- as described in the table below:
